reason: Rebekah, the matriarch and a leadership figure in the household, actively collaborates with Jacob throughout the passage. When Rebekah learns of Isaac's intention to bless Esau, she instructs Jacob on exactly what to do: obtain the goats, bring them to her, and follow her guidance in the deception. Jacob then works in concert with his mother—he fetches the goats, she prepares the food, she dresses him, and he executes the plan. Their cooperation and coordinated action to achieve the blessing for Jacob demonstrates clear collaboration between a leader (Rebekah) and those under her direction (Jacob) working together toward a shared objective.
